_comment: EXAMPLE · Kafka source with a SCHEMA REGISTRY, CHECKED. Registry mode is a property of the CONNECTION (connections/kafka_topic_in_registry.yaml sets schema_registry), not of the source — the @stream_publisher (functions/kafka_registry/read_registry_avro.py) is byte-identical to the registry-less Avro one in kafka_src. What changes is the wire: a registry message is [0x00][4-byte schema id][payload], the consumer fetches THAT schema version to decode it, and old messages keep decoding after the producer evolves. A PLAIN message on a registry topic fails to deserialize — everything `rpk topic produce` and the redpanda data plane write — and goes to the dead-letter topic, which is how a producer that is not registry-aware is caught. `schema` stays REQUIRED: it is cross-checked against the registry's resolved schema. The redpanda domain exports SCHEMA_REGISTRY_URL, interpolated PLAIN because an endpoint is a name, not a credential. STAGES: (1) the domain; (2) actions, tagged live -- scripts/produce_events.py writes 50 events through a registry-aware serializer (the schema registered under <prefix>.registry_events-value) and then 5 plain JSON events to the same topic, each appended to ${xp:dir}/ops.jsonl -- BEFORE the publisher subscribes, so the topic exists when it does (a consumer subscribed to a topic not there yet sees it only at its next metadata refresh, 5 minutes by default); (3) collections -- stream (the registry connection) and dead (kafka_registry_dead over <prefix>.registry_dead, plain JSON envelopes, its own connection); (4) functions; (5) actions, tagged check -- scripts/verify_kafka.py: the 50 in registry_events exactly once, the 5 plain ones as dead letters (--require-dead), polling at most 5m; (6) monitor. Run: `tdd xp one-shot --suite kafka/kafka_registry --keep`.
